title: SCE 3.3 Detective Probe — CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and CloudWatch Alarms Detect Full IMDS Attack Chain (T1578 + T1552.005 + T1078.004) [Two-Stack Architecture]
description: Validates that all three detective controls detect their respective attack steps within defined windows. The experiment uses a two-stack CloudFormation architecture to avoid the 1200-second provisioning timeout that caused the previous execution to fail: Stack A provisions the base infrastructure (VPC, NAT GW, EC2, IAM, Lambdas, S3, ECR, SSM) and Stack B provisions the observability layer (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, CloudWatch metric filters and alarms). AWS Config recorder has been replaced with a direct ec2:DescribeInstances state check to eliminate the primary timeout root cause. Step 1.2 (T1578): ec2:ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions weakens the test EC2 instance; detection verified by (a1) a CloudTrail management event in the trail CloudWatch Logs group and (a2) ec2:DescribeInstances confirming HttpTokens=optional and HopLimit=2. Step 2.2 (T1552.005): IMDSProbeFunction VPC Lambda issues an unauthenticated IMDSv1 curl to the instance; detection verified by (b1) VPC Flow Logs CloudWatch Alarm transitioning to ALARM on port-80 ACCEPT traffic and (b2) HarvestSignalParam SSM containing harvested:: prefix. Step 3.2 (T1078.004): SimulatedAttackerFunction assumes ExfiltrationSimRole and makes lateral-movement API calls; detection verified by (c1) CloudTrail log events from the ExfiltrationSimRole principal and (c2) TrailAlarm transitioning to ALARM. Pre-flight checks validate all stack outputs before proceeding; PreConditionError is raised on missing state rather than propagating KeyError.

steady-state-hypothesis.title: CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs CloudWatch Alarm, EC2 IMDS state change, and CloudWatch Trail Alarm all detect the three-step IMDS attack chain within defined detection windows
